innovation_proposals.title: Market-signal stack: add a spread-rate-of-change (wideningspeed) guard to the book-selection rule
innovation_proposals.rationale: The rule selects its book on BAA10Y LEVEL vs its 10y median (2.27 vs 2.59 = tight) and applies a 200d trend overlay only to the sleeves, not to the signal itself. A widening-speed guard (e.g., if BAA10Y 1-month change exceeds its own 90th percentile historically, defer to the defensive book or force the trend overlay to a shorter window) would have caught 2008, 2011, 2015-16 and 2020 spread regimes earlier. This is a claim about the RULE, not this month's reading, so it belongs in probation where FAVORS can measure it, not in the assessment field.

innovation_proposals.title: Audit the market-signal stack backtest-to-live drawdown divergence
innovation_proposals.rationale: The stack's confronted FAVORS record in falling-growth-falling-inflation shows maxDD -4.7% and calmar 5.05 over n=15, yet the live paper portfolio (ms-stack) has already realized -23.8% maxDD and calmar 0.155 since adoption — a 5x divergence on the risk metric the owner actually experiences. Either the backtest understates the concentrated books' path risk (sleeve construction, monthly decision cadence, trend-overlay lag in fast crashes like March 2020), or the FAVORS window is unrepresentative. If the confronted numbers are overstating the live risk envelope, every downstream consumer of those FAVORS rows — verdicts, ranking commentary, probation decisions — is leaning on a flattering mirror. This should be measured, not argued.

spec.audit_scope: ms-stack live NAV path vs backtested path for identical signal decisions since adoption
questions: Does the backtest apply the 200d trend overlay with the same knowable-at-date discipline as live?

Should FAVORS rows for the concentrated books carry a path-risk haircut until live and backtest reconcile?
